title: Retinal Microstructure Imaging Using OCT
author: David A. Antonetti
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yabfsan
materials: Animal is then sedated with ketamine and xylazine
Bioptigen Diver software is used to analyze retinal structure from the image obtained

steps.title: Dilate Animal Eyes
steps.instruction: Dilate the eyes of conscious animals using tropicamide and phenylephrine.

substeps.instruction: Apply a small drop (~10 µl) of 1% tropicamide.
Apply a small drop of 2.5% phenylephrine 2 to 3 minutes later.

steps.title: Prepare Animal for Imaging
steps.instruction: Sedate the animal and position it for the scan.

substeps.instruction: Keep corneas moist with wetting agents (Systane) after sedation.
Place the animal on a platform that enables three-dimensional fine movements.

steps.title: Configure Imaging System
steps.instruction: Adjust the camera lens to aim at the eye to acquire images without physical contact.

steps.title: Perform SD-OCT Imaging
steps.instruction: Obtain a volume or radial scan (1.4 x 1.4 mm) from each eye using a Bioptigen Envisu R2200 preclinical spectral domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) system.

steps.title: Post-Imaging Recovery
steps.instruction: Allow the animal to recover from the anesthesia after the imaging procedure.
